# ANALYSIS: TRENDLINE_BREAK_CALL_VETO_OOS_AB_TEST

**Filed:** 2026-07-17
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** OOS real-fills A/B test
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Enabling the TRENDLINE_BREAK_CALL_VETO gate will avoid call loser trades on 5/07 by vetoing CALL entries when a bearish structure break is detected, without affecting PUT winner trades on 4/29, 5/01, and 5/04. This is expected to increase edge_capture by approximately $165 (the sum of the two 5/07 call losses) while preserving all PUT winner P&L.

## Mechanism

The gate uses `market_structure.py` to detect a 5-minute close through a respected ascending support (trendline). When detected, it sets a `call_veto` flag. When the `call_veto` knob is enabled, the engine skips any CALL entry signal on that bar. The gate does not evaluate or affect PUT entries. Entry timing, contract selection, and exit logic remain unchanged for non-vetoed signals.

## Expected impact on OP-16 anchors

| J day | Current engine behavior | Proposed behavior (with call-veto enabled) | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4/29 winner | PUT winner taken (+$342) | PUT winner taken (+$342) | $0 |
| 5/01 winner | PUT winner taken (+$470) | PUT winner taken (+$470) | $0 |
| 5/04 winner | PUT winner taken (+$730) | PUT winner taken (+$730) | $0 |
| 5/05 loser | PUT loser taken (-$260) | PUT loser taken (-$260) | $0 |
| 5/06 loser | PUT loser taken (-$300) | PUT loser taken (-$300) | $0 |
| 5/07 loser 1 | CALL loser taken (-$45) | CALL entry vetoed → $0 | +$45 |
| 5/07 loser 2 | CALL loser taken (-$120) | CALL entry vetoed → $0 | +$120 |

*Note: The gate does not fire as a discriminating PUT trigger (fires on all 6 J dates equally), but as a CALL-veto it only affects CALL signals. On PUT days, the gate firing has no effect because no CALL entry is attempted. On 5/07, the gate fires before the J call entries (11:10 ET break vs. 11:15+ entries) and vetoes them.*

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+ account; $1K paper realizes ~14% of headline P&L. Test uses identical position sizing as baseline engine.
2. **Sample bias:** Full 16-month OOS window (2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18) used for real-fills validation, matching leaderboard methodology. Overfit risk mitigated by OOS holdout and walk-forward checks.
3. **Out-of-sample:** Will report OOS result post-test (currently NEEDS-OOS).
4. **Real-fills:** Will validate on top 3 J days (4/29, 5/01, 5/04 PUT winners; 5/07 CALL losers) using real OPRA fills (currently NEEDS-REAL-FILLS).
5. **Failure modes:** 
   - Worst day: Gate fails to fire on 5/07 → no delta (current -$165 call losses remain).
   - Max drawdown: Expected improvement from avoiding 5/07 losses; will measure post-test.
   - Blow-up: Excessive CALL vetoing on non-J days → potential missed winners; monitored via aggregate Sharpe and non-J day P&L.
6. **Concentration:** Will report top-5 days % of P&L for both arms; expect minimal change as impact is isolated to one loser day (5/07).

## Pre-merge gate

- Gym validators: All tests must pass (e.g., `backtest/tests/test_trendline_engine.py`).
- Walk-forward: OOS/IS Sharpe ratio ≥ 0.70 for call-veto enabled arm.
- Real-fills: Confirm avoidance of 5/07 CALL losers and preservation of 4/29/5/01/5/04 PUT winners on OPRA data.
- Aggregate: No significant degradation in edge_capture or Sharpe on non-J days (neutral or positive delta acceptable).

## Confidence

7 / 10 -- Timing validated (5/07 break precedes J call entries) and mechanistic plausibility high. Requires OOS real-fills confirmation to quantify exact impact and rule out adverse effects on non-J CALL/PUT dynamics.
